title: The Search for Extraterrestrial Life and Death

Just now

--

Jewish mothers are known for inciting a sense of guilt in their children. A popular tale holds it that after a Jewish mother was disappointed by the career accomplishments of her 36-year-old child, she complained: “By your age, Mozart did not only compose over 50 symphonies, but he even managed to die!”

The simplest assumption in physics is that similar circumstances lead to similar outcomes. It is therefore reasonable to assume that many intelligent species may have lived throughout cosmic history on the surface of Earth-like exoplanets which are positioned at a similar distance from Sun-like stars. By the present technological age of humanity, the most advanced among them did not only accomplish much more in interstellar travel than humanity did but they even managed to die! The technological products that space faring civilizations left behind outlive them, just like Mozart’s symphonies. It makes more sense to these even more than to search for their fleeting radio signals, which by now are long gone.

The duration of the radio transmission lifetime is a key inhibitor in the likelihood of detecting an extraterrestrial radio communication signal based on the Drake equation. The equivalent equation for spacecraft that are bound by gravity to the Milky-Way, sums the reservoir of technological relics. These interstellar objects accumulate over time, just like messages inside bottles traveling through the ocean of interstellar space.

The number of such messages in a bottle that reach our shores on Earth depends on whether Earth was targeted deliberately as an interesting destination. It also depends on whether any historical civilization out there produced self-replicated messengers. Dandelion flowers spread their genetic code in seeds that reproduce them when they land on fertile grounds after being carried by the wind. If nature manages to do it, surely synthetic biology or pure technology can manufacture such behavior by design. The carriers of these seeds could be interstellar objects that enter planetary systems nearly aligned with the orbital plane of the planets, as 3I/ATLAS did.

Whether the passages of interstellar objects in our past resulted in seeding the Earth with technological probes remains to be checked experimentally. This requires serious scientific work, not emotional tweets on social media.

The five tranches of data released by over the past four months in the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE) describe mysterious orbs and triangular-shaped objects as Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP). Whether all of them represent human-made technologies or some are messages in bottles from interstellar space will be decided through the scientific investigation conducted by the UAP Science Advisory Council (https://uapsac.com/).

Dogmatists argue that all UAP must be human-made, because this is the familiar paradigm that they followed throughout their career. The situation is similar to mainstream comet experts who argued here that the anomalous interstellar object `Oumuamua — which showed substantial non-gravitational acceleration without any outgassing, as summarized here, must be a `dark comet’ with an invisible coma and tail. Surely, there are comets which shed a tiny amount of gas and dust so that their coma and tail reflect sunlight at a faint level that is difficult to detect. However, if `Oumuamua was a comet — it had to lose about a tenth of its mass in order to gain its observed non-gravitational acceleration. Such a massive loss would have been difficult to miss near Earth for an iceberg of order a hundred meters in length, roughly the size of a football field.

Stating that `Oumuamua has an invisible tail is like saying “the emperor has invisible clothes” with an authority that is likely false or empty, but people collectively pretend otherwise out of fear, conformity, or self-interest. It highlights a state of collective denial or groupthink that could be suddenly shattered when someone has the courage to state the obvious truth. Gladly, whether we have had neighbors will not be settled by the consensus of comet experts but rather by scientific evidence.

In Hans Christian Andersen’s 1837 tale, two swindlers convince a vain emperor they’re weaving him a magnificent robe visible only to the wise and competent, and anyone who can’t see it must be a fool or unfit for their position. The emperor, his ministers, and the whole town play along, praising fabric that doesn’t exist, because admitting they see nothing would mean admitting inadequacy. It takes a child, with no stake in social performance, to simply say what’s true: “he has nothing on.” I follow that child in real life and do not care about what my Jewish mother would have advised about the risk to my career from saying that. Life is short and we better focus on substance.
